objective: Make intake, discussion, specification review, and post-discussion reconciliation explicit mandatory gates in every AWG oracle interaction lifecycle.
scope: Coordinator task identity and revision binding
versioned before and after work-plan and design-document references
user interaction evidence and explicit continue or unresolved disposition
assumptions: Coordinator remains authoritative for task identity, revision, dependencies, claims, and transitions
AWG owns the interaction-gate contract and AWQ validates its public evidence shape
Artifact references contain bounded public metadata, digests, and no private discussion content
The autonomous checker is deterministic and offline
unknowns: A future transport may choose a different storage format while preserving this record contract
Projects may add gate-specific evidence fields without weakening the required fields
invariants: All four mandatory gate types occur exactly once before lifecycle completion
Every gate is bound to the same current task revision as the lifecycle record
Every gate has versioned before and after work-plan and design-document references plus specification and formal-check references
Every gate records that interaction occurred and an explicit continue or unresolved disposition
A lifecycle with an unresolved contradiction cannot be marked complete
A stale task revision, failed formal check, missing gate, missing artifact, or unsafe reference fails closed
Oracle approval and formal evidence do not assert implementation correctness
acceptance_predicates: A complete synthetic lifecycle with all four gates passes the autonomous checker
Missing discussion or specification-review gates are rejected
Stale gate revisions and incomplete before or after artifacts are rejected
A complete lifecycle containing an unresolved contradiction is rejected
A gate explicitly marked unresolved remains non-complete and can be reopened
Private prompts, transcripts, absolute paths, and unbounded evidence are not accepted

formalization.scope: finite four-gate lifecycle records and hostile fail-closed fixtures
